quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually and do not brake.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You have a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down and adjust your speed for the curves ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A downgrade or hill is ahead.
Road construction area.
The road is getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downgrade or hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a steep downgrade or hill ahead. The hill may be long or steep, or it may have sharp curves.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
So the truck can stop safely.
To help other drivers slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck can stop safely.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more distance to stop than cars because they are heavier. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
A divided highway is starting.
The divided highway is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: The divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the divided highway ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes or move your position.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps straighten out the car.

questions.question: You have a green light but there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to cross first.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must let pedestrians in the intersection cross safely. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you do?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on the interstate. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down, move it completely off the traveled part of the road if you can.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are in or near a school zone. Watch for children and obey the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates. Wait until the gates lift and the tracks are clear, then proceed.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates. Wait until the gates lift and the tracks are clear, then proceed.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning lights, or flaggers alert you to a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events causes traffic congestion. Avoid this behavior.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road has curves ahead. Slow down as needed.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve function and body functions. It reduces judgment and your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
On the left of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center line. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Erratic and unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
Driving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Erratic and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers making erratic or unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest action is to move out of their way.

questions.question: Why should you use antifreeze washer fluid?

options.text: Cold fluid can scratch your windshield.
Moisture can cause cold wiper blades to crack.
It stops the washer fluid from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the washer fluid from freezing.
questions.explanation: Use antifreeze washer fluid when temperatures drop below freezing. You need it to clean salt, dirt, and slush from your windshield in winter.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual location, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked car does not become a hazard. Keep your vehicle visible to drivers coming from any direction.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights blind you while driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When blinded by oncoming headlights, look toward the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the other car.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the road center mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only in your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double yellow centerline means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: This sign indicates that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right, then curves left.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a yield sign is coming up. Start slowing down when you see this warning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Construction or maintenance work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or maintenance work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction, maintenance, and work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Traffic fines may double in these zones.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order for traffic lights?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers that traffic signals are at the next intersection.

questions.question: What do orange background signs indicate?

options.text: General warning signs.
Construction and maintenance warning signs.
Regulatory signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are only used for construction and maintenance warnings.
